prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
The `tasklist` extension is added and registered, so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` loads it by short name; the full suite passes (1151 tests, 112 skipped), including 22 new tests. flake8, the spellchecker and the docs build were not run (not installed here). Nothing is committed.

Behaviours you might not assume:
- With the default `xhtml` output the checkbox renders as `<input checked="checked" disabled="disabled" type="checkbox" />`; with `output_format='html'` it is `<input checked disabled type="checkbox">`.
- A marker with nothing after it (`- [x]`) is left as plain text, because the marker must be followed by a space.
- An empty `item_class` adds no class to the `<li>`.
- A task marker wins over a reference link of the same name (`[x]: url`) at the start of an item.

`docs/extensions/index.md` still says no new extensions will be added to the project; I added `tasklist` to the table there and left that note alone. The changelog entry is under a new `[Unreleased]` heading with no issue number, since there is no issue to reference.
